title: Closures and Iterators (Part 1) - Filter and transform
learning_objectives: Recognize closure syntax and use a closure where a function-like value is expected.
Create an iterator from a collection and apply common transformations.
Filter and transform values, then collect or aggregate the result.
Explain that iterator adapters are lazy until a consuming operation runs.
explanation: Closures are anonymous functions that can capture values from their environment. Iterators provide a composable way to process sequences: adapters such as `filter` and `map` describe work, and a consumer such as `collect` or `sum` performs it. This separation makes data-processing code concise without hiding its order of operations.

examples.title: Pass a closure to an operation
Filter, transform, and collect
Consume an iterator to perform its work

compiler_error_examples: error[E0308]: mismatched types; expected a reference, found an integer
completion_criteria: Exercise filters even values and squares them while preserving order
Learner can identify the filter, transformation, and consuming operations
Exercise handles both non-empty and empty input
